blocks.title: Background and motivation
blocks.content:
[]{#sec:Background and motivation label="sec:Background and motivation"}

Kashaev's [@Kashaev1997] proposes a striking connection between the geometry of hyperbolic knots and their quantum invariants. This conjecture appears to be related to quantum $\slg$ Chern-Simons theory, a TQFT arising as a complexification [@Gukov2005] or analytic continuation [@Witten2010] of the more familiar quantum $\operatorname{SU}(2)$ Chern-Simons theory [@zbMATH04092352]. Cyclic and principal type invariants

[]{#sec:negative type label="sec:negative type"}

There appear to be two inequivalent (but perhaps both natural) branches of complex Chern-Simons theory. Above we described invariants [@Baseilhac2004; @Bonahon2021; @Kashaev2005; @McPhailSnyderVolume] that

-   are defined as a sum over a finite state space,

-   are conjectured to exponentially grow as $N\to \infty$, and

-   are well-defined for any (or any geometrically non-degenerate) hyperbolic structure.

[]{#sub:Diagrams label="sub:Diagrams"}

::: definition
A of a knot $K$ is a representation $\rho \colon \pi_{1}(\comp{K}) \to \slg$ and a choice of eigenspace for the image of each peripheral subgroup of $K$ under $\rho$.
:::

blocks.title: Segment equations
blocks.content:
[]{#sec:Segment equations label="sec:Segment equations"}

The segment parameters have a natural geometric interpretation: they parametrize the locations of the ideal vertices of the octahedral decomposition. Following [@McphailSnyder2024octahedralcoordinateswirtingerpresentation] we obtained the segment parameters from a shadow coloring but one can also work in the opposite direction. An assignment of numbers $b_{i}$ to the segments of $D$ induces a decorated representation of $K$ if and only if the shape parameters satisfy Thurston's gluing equations.
